summary: Facts-and-defaults cross-check of release/6.1.0. I compared the same facts across README, docs/*.md (all sidebar pages), CHANGELOG [Unreleased], the knowledge topics, the prime template (templates/rules.ts), config/architecture schema templates, and live `--help` for all 26 commands and their subcommands. The facts covered were config defaults, provider model defaults, gitignore and gitattributes entries, file names, schema ids, exit codes, flag names, ports, counts and version numbers. Disputed facts were settled against source and the dev-container CLI (`yg init`, `yg init --provider codex`, `yg check`, `yg check --json`, `yg knowledge read configuration`, `yg prime`). These all agreed across surfaces and are not reported: schema ids (yg-check/1 and the rest), lock and state file names, the portal port 4317, the simulate default of 20 commits, drill exit codes, parallel=1, max_prompt_chars=50000, timeout=300, the tier regex, Node 22+, the example counts, the knowledge and schemas topic names, and every documented `yg <cmd> --flag` (a scripted check against live help found no unknown flags). Eleven findings survived verification and are listed below. The items already in flight were excluded.

surviving.title: Default reviewer model for claude-code is stated three ways, and the CLI's own error message contradicts the docs
surviving.where: source/cli/src/cli/init-reviewer-setup.ts:381-388; source/cli/src/io/config-parser.ts:182-186; docs/getting-started.md:74; docs/cli-reference.md:1655; docs/configuration.md:192; source/cli/src/templates/knowledge/configuration.ts:130-141; `yg init --help`
surviving.evidence: Runtime fallback, config-parser.ts:182-186: `PROVIDER_DEFAULTS = { 'claude-code': { model: 'haiku' }, 'codex': { model: 'o4-mini' }, 'gemini-cli': { model: 'gemini-2.5-flash' } }`. configuration.md:192 says the same ('Omitted on a CLI provider it defaults to: claude-code → haiku, codex → o4-mini, gemini-cli → gemini-2.5-flash'). But getting-started.md:74 says '`--model` defaults to `sonnet` for the `claude-code` provider only; every other provider requires `--model` explicitly', and `yg init --help` says '--model <name> Reviewer model (defaults to sonnet for claude-code; required otherwise)'. The live check `yg init --provider codex` in $TMPDIR/facts-b exited 2 with: 'Error: --model is required for provider 'codex'. Only claude-code has a built-in default model (sonnet); other providers must name the model explicitly.' That sentence is false against config-parser.ts, where codex and gemini-cli do have built-in defaults and claude-code's runtime default is haiku, not sonnet. Only knowledge/configuration.ts:139-141 explains that the two are different mechanisms.
surviving.impact: An adopter who reads getting-started or the init error and writes `provider: claude-code` by hand without `model:` believes the reviewer is Sonnet, but the rules are judged by Haiku. The tier name is the only reviewer fact folded into the hash, so nothing is re-verified and nothing reports the difference. The init refusal for codex and gemini-cli also contradicts the configuration page, which says those providers work without a model.
surviving.suggested_fix: Choose one default per provider and use it in both init-reviewer-setup.ts and PROVIDER_DEFAULTS; making init write what the runtime would use anyway is the simplest option. Until then, reword the init error to something like 'init requires --model for <provider>', drop the 'Only claude-code has a built-in default' claim, and make getting-started.md:74 and cli-reference.md:1655 say that the init default (sonnet) and the runtime fallback (haiku) differ.
surviving.verifier: Reproduced. In the container, `yg init --provider codex` printed "Only claude-code has a built-in default model (sonnet); other providers must name the model explicitly." It exited 1, not the 2 the finding claims. config-parser.ts:182-186 has PROVIDER_DEFAULTS claude-code→haiku, codex→o4-mini and gemini-cli→gemini-2.5-flash, so the error's 'why' line is false. init also writes `model: sonnet` while the runtime fallback is haiku. The impact is overstated, though. getting-started.md:74 and cli-reference.md:1655 describe the `--model` flag of init, and for that flag they are accurate. configuration.md:192 correctly documents the runtime fallback. knowledge/configuration.ts:139-141 explicitly separates the two mechanisms. A reader does not come away thinking hand-written config runs Sonnet. What is actually wrong is one false error sentence and two defaults for the same provider that are never cross-referenced on the docs site. That is friction, not a wrong model.

surviving.title: Interactive `yg init` asks the user to type the API key in a visible field; the docs say the key is read only from an environment variable
surviving.where: docs/getting-started.md:30-38 vs source/cli/src/cli/init-reviewer-setup.ts:55-65, 204-208, 221-224
surviving.evidence: getting-started.md:30-38 describes the interactive walk: 'The API providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google) need a key, read only from an environment variable (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `GOOGLE_API_KEY` — never a flag, so it never lands in shell history)'. In code, the interactive flow always calls `apiKey = await promptApiKey(provider)` (line 207) and never checks `process.env` first. `promptApiKey` uses `p.text({ message: `API key for ${provider}${hint}`, ... validate: (v) => ((v ?? '').trim().length === 0 ? 'API key cannot be empty' : undefined) })`. So the key is typed into a plain, echoed text field, not `p.password`. The hint says '(or set ${envVar} env var)', but an empty answer is rejected even when that variable is set. Only the non-interactive path (lines 410-411) reads the environment variable. Everything the docs say about 'env-only' credentials (cli-reference.md:1658, knowledge cli-reference.ts:1410) is true for `--provider` only.
surviving.impact: A user who follows the page expects the key to come from the environment. Instead init asks them to type it, shows it on screen (and in any terminal recording or pairing session), and refuses to continue until they do, even with the variable exported. The written documentation is wrong about how the default interactive path handles a secret.
surviving.suggested_fix: In the interactive flow, read the provider's environment variable first and ask only when it is missing, using `p.password`. Allow an empty answer when the variable is set, as the hint already promises. Or, if prompting is intentional, rewrite getting-started.md:35-38 to say the key is asked for interactively and stored in yg-secrets.yaml.
surviving.verifier: Confirmed in source. The interactive path calls `promptApiKey(provider)` unconditionally at init-reviewer-setup.ts:207 and again after a 401 at :222. `promptApiKey` (:55-65) uses `p.text` (echoed input, not `p.password`), and its validate rejects an empty value even though the hint reads '(or set ${envVar} env var)'. Only `resolveReviewerConfigFromFlags` (:407-411) reads process.env. getting-started.md:35-38 says of the interactive walk that the key is 'read only from an environment variable ... never a flag'. For the default interactive path the docs are wrong, and a secret is echoed on screen. This is not on the in-flight list; the in-flight item about init --provider covers probing and comments only.

surviving.title: The `.yggdrasil/.gitignore` entry list differs on four surfaces; the knowledge copy lacks the rotation glob that keeps refusal text out of git

surviving.evidence: Live `yg init` in $TMPDIR/facts-a writes 13 lines: `yg-secrets.yaml .symbols-cache/ .ast-cache/ .type-class-cache/ .debug.log .yg-lock.deterministic.json .yg-events.jsonl* .yg-fill-divergence.log* .feature-field.json .family-candidates.json .family-candidates.*.json .yg-packages-versions.json *.tmp`. The docs/configuration.md table has 11 entries and omits both family-candidates lines, which this release added (CHANGELOG: 'yg init and yg adopt now gitignore every family-candidates file'). The live `yg knowledge read configuration` (§Local state, lines 334-345) lists only 9, written as `.yg-events.jsonl` and `.yg-fill-divergence.log` without the trailing `*`, and omits `.yg-packages-versions.json`, `*.tmp` and both family-candidates lines. Yet init-scaffold.ts:114-118 says the `.yg-events.jsonl*` line is 'matching ... what `yg knowledge read configuration` states is ignored', and adds that the rotation 'keeps a refusal's full reason text, so a rotation must never become committable'. The tutor playbook onboarding.ts:327-334 tells the agent to hand-write the list 'so the derived caches ... never surface as untracked files and break the porcelain proof', but omits both family-candidates lines.
surviving.impact: An agent or adopter who writes the gitignore from the knowledge topic leaves `.yg-events.jsonl.1` (full refusal reasons, which can contain code fragments) committable. It also leaves the package-version cache and orphaned temp files untracked. surviving.suggested_fix: Generate the list in both knowledge topics and in the docs table from `YGGDRASIL_GITIGNORE_LINES`, or add a test asserting they are equal. surviving.verifier: The drift is real. A live `yg init` in $TMPDIR/verify-facts-and-defaults-a wrote 13 lines, including `.yg-events.jsonl*`, both family-candidates lines, `.yg-packages-versions.json` and `*.tmp`. The configuration.md table (:407-419) omits both family-candidates lines. `yg knowledge read configuration` lists `.yg-events.jsonl` with no `*` (line 341) and omits .yg-packages-versions.json, *.tmp and the family-candidates lines, although the init-scaffold.ts:114-118 comment claims the knowledge topic matches. onboarding.ts:327-334 keeps the `*` globs but omits the family-candidates lines. The severity is overstated. The knowledge block describes what init writes; it does not tell anyone to hand-write the list, and init itself always writes the full set. The only hand-write path is onboarding, which already has the rotation globs. What is left is stale documentation plus one gap in a tutorial recipe. That is minor.

surviving.title: packages.md contradicts itself on whether `yg pack update` without a name can leave some packages updated, and its 'unreachable source' row is too strong
surviving.where: docs/packages.md:81-85 vs 192-195 and table row at 394; source/cli/src/cli/pack.ts:751-829
surviving.evidence: packages.md:81-85: '`yg pack update` with no name checks every installed copy before it replaces any of them, so an edited file under one package stops the whole run with nothing touched — not the package you edited and not the ones sorting before it.' packages.md:194-195, same page: 'With no package named, that refusal stops a run that has already updated everything sorting before the drifted package.' The code matches the first statement. pack.ts:753-762 checks drift for every package before the loop, and the refusal's why says 'Nothing was updated — not this package and not any other'. The table row at :394 says 'The source cannot be reached | Nothing is installed or changed, and nothing is left behind'. But the update loop (pack.ts:789-829) fetches and installs one package at a time, and `installPackage` writes the lock on each pass. If the source for a later package cannot be fetched, the packages already replaced stay replaced.
surviving.impact: A reader cannot tell what state their repository is in after a refused update. One paragraph is wrong about drift. The table misstates the one case that really is partial: a source that becomes unreachable partway through a multi-package update.
surviving.suggested_fix: Delete the sentence at 194-195. Qualify the table row: an unreachable source leaves that package untouched, but packages earlier in the same no-name run keep their update. Alternatively, fetch every source before installing any, so the row becomes true.
surviving.verifier: Confirmed. packages.md:81-85 says nothing is touched. packages.md:194-195 says a run 'has already updated everything sorting before the drifted package'. pack.ts:753-782 judges drift for all packages before the loop, and its refusal says 'Nothing was updated', so :194-195 is stale. The table row 'The source cannot be reached | Nothing is installed or changed' is too strong for a multi-package run. The loop (pack.ts:789-829) fetches and installs one package at a time, and `fetchSource` (pack.ts:197ff) calls `failWith` ('Could not reach ...') partway through, so earlier packages stay updated. Each package install is still atomic and the lock stays consistent with disk, so no data is lost. The problem is a wrong description of the state a refused run leaves behind, not a costly defect. Downgraded to minor.

summary: Terminology audit of Yggdrasil release/6.1.0 docs. I read the VitePress sidebar in order (how-it-works → getting-started → aspects/nodes/relations → author pages → the-lock/family-contracts), then README, CHANGELOG [Unreleased], the yg prime rules template (source/cli/src/templates/rules.ts), the knowledge topics, the portal glossary (glossary.js, state-model.js) and `yg check --help`. I also ran the live CLI in a scratch project inside the container, using `yg context --file/--node`, `yg check --approve`, `yg check --json` and `yg aspects`, to see which words actually reach users. The core nouns node, flow, port, relation, mapping and lock are used consistently. The drift sits in the words that describe judging and coverage: 'reviewer' has four meanings, 'approve/verified' covers both running a review and passing one, 'covered' covers both 'mapped' and 'has a rule', 'tier' has three senses, and 'family' and 'file-level' are each used for unrelated things. Several core terms are defined only on the last sidebar page and there is no glossary. I left out everything on the in-flight list: yg verdict, pair/lock undefined in getting-started, the 'unverified' label and the CI recipe.
